title: Two token-screening gates can never fire: the anti-bot selector scan matches "0x"-prefixed selectors that cannot occur inside bytecode, and the blocklist is always empty

evidence.note: isBlacklistedTokenForChain: bytecode.includes("0xdd62ed3e") etc. The bytecode string has a single "0x" at its start, so the test is false for every real token (true only on an RPC error)
0xdd62ed3e is allowance(address,address), which every ERC20 has; simply stripping the prefix would make the gate block every token
BLOCKLIST tokens/pairs are empty Sets; nothing in src adds to them
V2 blocklist checks against the empty sets
isKnownBadTokenForChain: only "no code" or the empty blocklist; the creator check is skipped
alert prints "Blacklist Function" from the no-op gate
codex (22-27 independent second opinion, graded S2): Blacklist selector scanning includes an impossible interior 0x prefix

sibling_sites_checked: Both blacklist scanners (tokenSafety.ts:56-61 legacy, :331-340 chain) and every BLOCKLIST use (bot.ts:889, :895, :1218; tokenSafety.ts:204, :441) checked; git grep found no code that adds to BLOCKLIST. The bytecode scan is AUD-BUY-014.
severity_rationale: S2: two gates in the buy path are no-ops, so the alert line "Blacklist Function: No" is printed for every token and the "known bad token" gate only rejects addresses with no code. The bytecode mutability scan (honeypot/bytecodeScan.ts) independently covers setBlacklist-style selectors, which bounds the effect.
recommendation: Either make each gate test what it is named for (strip the prefix, drop the allowance selector, give the blocklist a data source) or remove it and stop printing its result. Fixing it would block more tokens, so it is a behaviour change on card BUY-05. Phase 24 or 29 per the card.
